summary:
AgroTwin AI is an agricultural intelligence platform designed to help farmers and agricultural stakeholders make more informed and sustainable decisions in response to climate change. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data,” the platform combines NASA Earth observation data with geospatial tools to explore agricultural land and better understand environmental conditions.

Users can explore geographic areas through an interactive map, draw and measure agricultural plots, calculate land areas, register crops, and access climate information such as temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation using NASA POWER data. The platform also supports the organization of agricultural records and the export of plot and crop information in CSV format. Additionally, it provides a foundation for exploring agricultural scenarios by connecting environmental information with land characteristics and crop data.

AgroTwin AI addresses the growing challenges of climate variability, changing rainfall patterns, water availability, and environmental pressures on agriculture. By making Earth observation data more accessible and easier to interpret, the project aims to support more informed decisions, encourage sustainable farming practices, and contribute to more resilient agricultural systems.
details:
1. Project Overview

AgroTwin AI is an interactive agricultural intelligence platform designed to connect Earth observation data, geospatial analysis, and agricultural information to support more informed farming decisions. Its goal is to help farmers and agricultural stakeholders better understand their land and explore how environmental conditions can influence agricultural activities.

2. How Does It Work?

The platform provides an interactive map where users can explore geographic areas, identify agricultural land, and draw or edit field boundaries. Using geospatial tools, users can measure their agricultural plots and calculate their total area in hectares.

Users can also register crops and access environmental information, including temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation through NASA POWER data. These variables help users explore local climate conditions and understand environmental factors that may affect agricultural production.

AgroTwin AI brings these elements together in a digital agricultural environment, providing a foundation for exploring agricultural scenarios and comparing environmental information with land and crop characteristics.

The scenario exploration feature allows users to organize and review factors related to crop rotation and environmental conditions. It is designed as a qualitative planning aid and does not generate automatic or scientifically validated agronomic recommendations. Its purpose is to help users consider relevant information before making decisions with appropriate local knowledge and expert guidance.

3. Benefits and Expected Impact

AgroTwin AI aims to make satellite-based environmental information and geospatial tools more accessible to agricultural users. Its main benefits include:

  • Improving access to climate and Earth observation information.
  • Supporting the identification, mapping, and measurement of agricultural plots.
  • Helping users understand environmental conditions that influence farming.
  • Organizing geographic, climate, and crop information in one platform.
  • Encouraging more informed and sustainable agricultural planning.

The expected impact is to contribute to more resilient agricultural systems, especially in regions where climate variability, changing rainfall patterns, and water availability create challenges for farmers.

4. Technologies and Tools

AgroTwin AI was developed using modern web technologies and open-source tools:

  • React: For building the interactive user interface.
  • Vite: For frontend development and production builds.
  • Python: For backend development and data processing.
  • FastAPI: For creating the application's API and connecting the frontend with backend services.
  • SQLite: For storing application information.
  • Leaflet: For interactive geographic maps.
  • Leaflet-Geoman: For drawing and editing geographic areas.
  • Turf.js: For geospatial calculations and area measurements.
  • NASA POWER: For accessing environmental and climate-related data.
  • React Leaflet: For integrating interactive maps into the React interface.
  • Tailwind CSS: For styling the user interface and application components.
  • Lucide: For interface icons and visual elements.
  • HTML: For structuring the web application.
  • JavaScript: For frontend functionality and interactive features.
  • JSON: For structuring and exchanging data between application components.

These technologies allow the platform to combine geographic visualization, environmental information, and agricultural data in a single web application.

5. Innovation and Creativity

The innovative aspect of AgroTwin AI is its approach to bringing together NASA Earth observation data, interactive geographic mapping, and agricultural information in a digital environment.

Instead of presenting environmental data as isolated numbers, the platform connects climate information with the geographic areas and crops that users want to explore. This makes complex environmental information easier to visualize and understand.

The project establishes a foundation for an agricultural digital twin approach, where geographic and environmental information can help users explore different agricultural conditions and planning scenarios.

6. Factors Considered by the Team

During development, the team considered the importance of climate variability, agricultural sustainability, access to environmental information, and the need for accessible digital tools.

The project emphasizes the use of open NASA data, geographic visualization, and a user-friendly interface. It also recognizes that satellite-derived information has spatial and temporal limitations and should complement, rather than replace, local observations and soil measurements.

AgroTwin AI aims to demonstrate how space-based data and accessible technology can help address real agricultural challenges and support a more sustainable future.

NASA GIBS Imagery Acknowledgment

We acknowledge the use of imagery provided by services from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), part of NASA's Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS).
